title: Concept-Residual Representation Expansion for Robustness to Spurious Correlations

problem.claim: ERM-trained models can rely on non-causal correlations that fail when the training correlation changes or disappears.

gap.claim: Robust core features may be weak or entangled within ERM representations, making them difficult to identify despite evidence that useful robust features remain.

contributions.claim: The paper proposes Concept-Residual eXpansion, a concept-augmented framework for improving robustness by expanding candidate predictive features.
CRX augments a frozen ERM representation with interpretable task-relevant concept scores and residual features capturing ERM information not expressed by those concepts.
CRX retrains a lightweight classifier on the expanded feature space containing structured semantic cues and complementary residual information.

author_reported_evidence.claim: On standard benchmarks for spurious correlations, CRX consistently raises worst-group accuracy while retaining competitive average performance.
The authors report that expanding the available feature set can substantially improve robustness to spurious correlations.
The authors report that code and additional implementation details are available through the linked Zenodo record.

narrative_sequence.summary: ERM models may exploit spurious correlations that do not generalize beyond the training environment.
Robust features may remain available but be weak or entangled in the learned representation.
CRX expands frozen ERM representations with concept scores and residual features, then trains a lightweight classifier.
The authors report improved worst-group accuracy with competitive average performance on standard benchmarks.
The reported results support feature-set expansion as a way to improve robustness to spurious correlations.

source_observation.claim: Adding interpretable concept scores and residual information to a frozen ERM representation is reported to improve worst-group accuracy.

interpretation.claim: Robustness may benefit from expanding accessible predictive information rather than only suppressing suspected spurious features.

application.claim: For models affected by changing correlations, evaluate lightweight classifiers over representations augmented with task-relevant semantic cues and residual features.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this approach works beyond the reported standard spurious-correlation benchmarks.

unknowns: The specific benchmark datasets, tasks, and metrics are not identified.
No quantitative performance values or comparison baselines are provided.
The method for obtaining interpretable concept scores is not specified.
The abstract does not report computational cost, failure cases, or sensitivity to concept quality.
